utterances.speaker: MR. VELIC
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will now mark that position with yellow spray paint. Please walk to and stand where the rubbish was, to the best of your recollection, on the day that you were shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. VELIC
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: Please stand at each end of where you recall the front of the first UNPROFOR vehicle and the back of the second UNPROFOR vehicle were positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VELIC
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will now mark that position with a yellow line. I will now mark this position with a yellow line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were given certain directions by the investigator. Did you comply with those directions truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did comply strictly to the directions. I just didn't show the proper distance between the two UNPROFOR vehicles. They were a little longer, so I apologise for that. The distance might have been greater now that I look back. They took up more space, both these vehicles, more space than I actually thought to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any event, towards the beginning of the video, when we first saw you standing alongside the investigator and indicating where your vehicle was at the relevant time, which direction was your vehicle facing at the time you were shot? Was it facing directly away from the camera or towards the camera or to one side or what?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: You want me to say where the camera was?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Velic. I'll withdraw that question. You may have had some difficulty in following me. I want to ask you where the front-end loader was facing at the time that you were shot. Could you tell us which direction it was facing, having regard to what we have just seen on the video as to the surrounding street scene?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. You noticed that very well, and let me explain. I have already explained where the rubbish dump was, and so the loader goes first, and then it goes back the way it came, and then moves in a circle towards the right. It is a machine that has a joint. The cabin stays facing one way, whereas the fork and loader can turn round in a circle and then can pick up -- can unload the rubbish. So if you look at it from my left-hand side, my left-hand door was turned towards Vrace. There is a small tree that went there at the time. It was just an open space. But the tree was planted after the country reintegrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. We will come back to that. In the meantime, I ask that the witness be shown three photographs, which are P3279DD. It appears that Madam Registrar does not have those. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, would you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President I just wish to indicate two things. The first is, as I have already said, the information system does not function perfectly with respect to the disk we have received. Secondly, we have just received this material, which means that it was impossible for us to show General Galic the documents, and this is not the first time that we have confronted -- been confronted with a situation where we are shown documents during the hearing and not beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if my friend has a problem with those photographs, I withdraw them. I can assure you, Mr. President, that my friend was given notice by letter of the exhibit number. I regret that we have overlooked to provide copies of those photographs. Perhaps at the next break, my friend could indicate to the Trial Chamber whether he has any problem with me continuing with those photographs in examination-in-chief, but at this stage, I withdraw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they will now be withdrawn for the moment, as far as I understand. Am I correct in -- when I read what is attached to your letter of the 27th of January, when I look at Ramiz Velic, I do not see any number 3279DD on it. Is that correct or -- let me just look at the letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have my case manager with me at the moment. Perhaps when I re-present the photographs, I will invite my friend to indicate if he is disadvantaged by them. I can indicate then which letter advised the Defence of the exhibit number, but I understand they were so advised. I will check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please check that? And so for this moment, I do understand that you withdraw this moment the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please see whether during the next break, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether there will be an opportunity to see what -- how important it is to discuss the matter with your client and -- well, we'll see whether there will be an opportunity to -- for you to confer with General Galic, and I will be informed by the Prosecution on when actually it was indicated to the Defence that this exhibit will be used, since there are two issues. The first one is putting the exhibit on the list, and the second issue is providing the Defence with a copy of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And that's quite distinct from the issue of disclosure. They were disclosed last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To assist my learned colleagues, I refer them to the supplemental information sheet, the English version, page 02131847. They will see there some relevant information to those photographs and the taking of the photographs. In the meantime, Mr. President, if may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown, and might we all view Exhibit 3279 D? That is the 360 degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the scene in front of you now, Mr. Velic, which for the transcript is a view looking along a road with what appears to be a four-storey-plus-ground-floor building on the right-hand side and a multi-storey series of buildings on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: That's the spot I was wounded, the former Brace Ribara Street. It used to be called the Trg Heroje or Heroes' Square, as I've already indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please pan the image to the left. Pause there for a moment. We now see a T-intersection with a street going off to the left. Do you recognise the area of the T-intersection?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that the area that you indicated on the video which we viewed a few minutes ago, that is the position of the rubbish that you were collecting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue to pan the photograph to the left. You mentioned Vrace in your evidence. If you see Vrace, please indicate that. Please continue to pan the photograph. Pause there for a moment. For the benefit of the transcript we see some trees in silhouette on the foot path and a parking area between two multi-storey buildings, and what appears to be some construction in the distance between the two buildings and also between the trees. Mr. Velic, do you know what area lay behind the trees in the distance? In other words, if you stood on the other side of the trees and looked in the direction away from the camera and between the two buildings, what would you see?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, across the stadium, you could look towards Vrace, and there was the MUP school, the school for MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And what is or was MUP?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The academy for training members of the MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does "MUP" stand for?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You say it's an academy for training members of MUP units?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And who graduated from the academy? What -- people in what occupation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: They were called policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Before the war, and it's still working now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you aware as to where the confrontation lines were approximately -- I withdraw that question. Do you know what side of the confrontation lines the academy was at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The academy was on the side of the former Republika Srpska, their army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What about the stadium at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: And the stadium, but not all of it; just part of the stadium, as far as I heard. I think that part of the stadium was right by the woods and the Tranzit Road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might we return to the 360-degree photograph, please. Do you remember whether, at the time you were shot, the trees which appear in that photograph on the footpath were there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't. All the trees were cut down, in the whole of the town, for firewood, and these trees were planted sometime in 1995. I know that they brought in some larger trees first, because I dug the holes and helped the people doing this work. But no, the trees weren't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please continue panning the photograph to the left. All right. Thank you. That might stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, what were you wearing on that day that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I was wearing some black corduroy trousers and a leather driver's jacket, the kind that us drivers were issued for winter. I'm not sure whether I had a cap on my head or not. I had a jumper underneath the jacket. It was rather a thick jumper, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What colour was the front-end loader, or colours?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: It was yellow, and all the construction machinery was usually yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you been shot at on any previous occasion whilst driving a front-end loader and collecting rubbish?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It happened on the 1st of November. It was down by the Olympic Games parking. We were also collecting rubbish down there, and also there was UNPROFOR present. There were APCs and soldiers. There were Dutch soldiers. And this other day when I was working, these were Egyptians. So before that day when I was wounded, also collecting rubbish, we also had security. It was from the student hall, from Nedzarici. There were two shots that came. I was facing them. There was a very large loader, 2 metres 70. Two cubic metres of water can fit into that loader. And I, in fact, did not hear the shots, but the young men who were with me, they heard the shots and then they told me -- my nickname is Cigo, and they told me, "Cigo, move away." So the Dutch returned fire, and then the shooting stopped and then we collected the rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You've said that that happened on the 1st of November. In what year?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Also in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown three photographs. They're marked P3244, 3245, and 3250.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, would you please look at the photograph which has marked at the top of it the numbers, in red, top right-hand corner, 02065063.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the record, that's P3244.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise yourself in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time that photograph was taken, were you standing approximately in the area where your vehicle was positioned when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's apparent from the time that this photograph was taken, one can see more of the gap between the two buildings, that is, more towards Vrace. Is that the case? There is less tree cover.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, drawing your attention to the gap between the two buildings, do you see what appear to be some stadium lights, that is, a tower with -- top of a tower with --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You earlier mentioned that the stadium was through there. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the right and lower than the top of the lights, there appears to be some concrete construction. What is that building?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: It is the cover of the stadium. This is where the standing area of the stadium is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please look at the photocopy of that same photograph, and by that I mean a black-and-white photocopy. Do you see some red markings on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you have written some words on the photograph as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you circled yourself and printed your name along that circling?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To the right, and indicated by the letter "B," there appears some writing. What is that writing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: There is a circle and then there is an arrow, and what I believed to have been the aggressor's positions, the positions of the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What appears within that red circle that you drew?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: You can see the MUP school there, and also a small field above the Zelja's stadium, above. And what can also be seen is a wood above the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I draw your attention back to the colour photograph, where we have some more detail. In the area that you circled in the black and white, you can see that there are some white, long, what appear to be buildings, and then above and behind them some red buildings. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you indicate, by reference to colours and shape, the MUP academy? And perhaps at the same time you could point to --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- that building on the -- using the metal pointer on the photograph to your right. That way, Mr. Velic, we can all see what you're pointing at.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can't see it very well. Yes, it's here, but I can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Can you see --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just a moment. Yes, this is it. Yes, this is where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please look at photograph -- the remaining photograph, which, for the record, is P3250. Does that appear to be a telephoto of the photograph you've just been looking at?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, perhaps, Mr. Usher, you could place that photograph on the -- it is already on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, could you turn now to the copy of that photograph to your right on the machine, and are you able to point out in that photograph the MUP academy?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: There. Approximately there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you indicating the building immediately behind the tree and to the top of the collection of buildings which are visible; indeed, the top building? Is that the one you mean to indicate?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, this long building there. Yes, there is a whole line of buildings there, MUP buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please take a marker -- blue marker?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you use the blue marker, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And would you carefully outline the buildings which were the academy, and if you like, so that you have the benefit of colour, you might also refer to the photograph -- the other photograph which shows you standing on the road with your hands on your hips. Mr. Velic, have you marked the photograph yet with the blue marker?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Take your time.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can do it. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Might those photographs be returned? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, during the conflict, were there cease-fires from time to time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. When something like that happened, this news happened, when cease-fires happened, we were very happy, but they were not really observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember what the situation is in relation to the day you were wounded, that is whether or not there was a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in what area of Sarajevo were you living in November of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: From 1992 -- sorry, from 1962, I have been working -- living in Cengic Vila, it's an area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what street?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: It is Bulevar Mese Selimovica 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there an incident which occurred in November of 1992, close to where you live, involving a shelling?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, it was -- I believe it was summer. There was a shop, it was a hair-dressing shop in our building, and we often -- the men from the neighbourhood came there to chat, and also those who were just passing by, and my eldest son was there as well. There were quite a few of us from the building, there were young people, and the shell hit, and we all had this instinct to rush to the site, to see whether someone had been wounded. So we all went there, including the young people, and my son went there, and I tried to stop him because they say often if one shell falls, another one will follow. So because there were also lower buildings next to the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If I can just ask to you pause there for a moment, what season do you think it was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Summer, I think, I believe it was summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the building where you lived one that had a number of storeys to it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It has 17 floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At any stage during the conflict, was there a period when you did not have running water in the apartment? That is in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Of course. This was throughout the conflict. We had shortage of water, electricity, heating.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there elevators in the apartment block?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. The lifts existed. There was one for odd and even floors each, but of course they did not work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that because of a lack of electricity, they didn't work?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Of course. The entire city had no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that throughout the apartment block, the 17 storeys, 17 floors, rather, that there was no running water. How did you and your fellow occupants, your neighbours, obtain water?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: We had -- we took canisters with us to where there was a water collection point, and as that happened, we had to go all the way to the brewery, which is about two, three kilometres perhaps in one way, and then whoever was brave would go to the Miljacka River and would fetch water from the river for bathroom purposes, sanitary purposes, but we somehow managed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I want to take you back to the incident where you were wounded, and the photograph that you viewed on your computer screen, and indeed, the photographs that you've seen in front of you. On the computer screen and in the photographs that were placed in front of you, you've seen a view towards Vrace, in particular a gap between two high-rise buildings as viewed from the position where your vehicle was at the time you were shot. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the time you were shot, what part of your vehicle faced that gap between the two buildings?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The left side, where the door is. That's the only side you can get in through, because on the right-hand side, you had all the control for the lever, for the loader. There were only just two commands. So it's hard to get in on that side. It's the left side that was facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You explained to us the position of your hand at the time that it was hit. What was immediately alongside your hand in that position, to the left? In other words, what part of the vehicle, if any?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, I can explain it. Say that this represents a steering wheel, and the steering wheel was in the height of my chest, so about this height.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, if I could just stop you for a moment, please, we cannot all see what it is that you are showing with the cord, so we will approach it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You've told us that you were in the cabin of the front-end loader when you were shot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that there was a door to your left and a door to your right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the door immediately to the left, that is the door area or the door space, immediately to the left of your left hand at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any opening in the door or was it entirely constructed of solid material?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No. The cabin is entirely made of tin. I'm not quite sure how thick it is, possibly .2 millimetres, but it is a double construction, the frames, and considering that one, the person who is operating the machine, has to have a good view, the cabin itself and the door are mostly made of glass or a type of plastified glass which was a usual thing. This is what we did in our workshops.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And apart from the glass, was there any other material used in the construction of the door? In other words, was the door entirely glass or partly glass, normally?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: It's the door like any other door. It had a frame and then there is the -- it's the glass is framed by a frame. It is on the photograph. And since there was no glass, but plexiglass, and then it tore, it broke, so the glass broke and so we had to put plexiglass, but both the front and the back screens were the sort of reinforced glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you opened the door, from a position of being inside the cabin, did the door open outwards or inwards?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Outwards. Both doors opened outwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And when the door swung out, would you be swinging out a frame which consisted entirely within the frame of plexiglass or was there some other material as well?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Just that part of the plexiglass frame is opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. What about the lower part of the door? What was that made from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The lower part of the door is just tin, about 25 centimetres, not very high. That's what the tin is. On some vehicles, it was also glass but I cannot remember. It was normally plexiglass but I don't think so. So the door is entirely made of this -- this plexiglass.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to say whether the bullet that hit your hand came through a doorway or a different part of the cabin?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I think the bullet came on the frame between the front screen and the door, through the tin, and through the plexiglas, at the height of the steering wheel and my hand, right in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness be shown Exhibit P1806.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, do you recognise that document which is in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is a letter of discharge from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you first see that document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: When I was discharged from the hospital, I had it with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How did you come to have it? Did someone give it to you? Who gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: As I was being discharged from hospital, I was given this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Just to make sure, because we received the same document in Serbian, two copies, and I don't know whether that's normal. We have two of them attached, in Serbian, and I do not have the impression that the -- possibly there is -- one copy is missing, because we have two copies with the same text, in Serbian, apparently. This is just to make sure, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I see a difference between the two Serbian copies, which is not on the text, but as far as the signature is concerned. So I don't know whether this would clarify the issue. I'm also looking to Mr. Ierace. I see on the right bottom part of the second page of the Serbian version, which seems to be a copy of the same document as on the first page, that there is a signature, or at least some handwriting, which, at least for me, makes the two copies distinct. And I can imagine that since it's just the signature that's different, that there's just one translation. If that's the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We can see the same number, in fact. And I'm trying to be very specific. We can see the same ERN number at the bottom of the page, the same number again, 00284231, and then the same number on the second. But as you can see, one has a signature and the other one doesn't. So I'm not sure whether we are talking about the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, am I right in understanding that the first page and the second page are the same document, one of them with some handwriting, signatures on it and the other not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You are, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the same document in different versions, one with, one without handwriting in the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just for clarity's sake: From the transcript -- how come that we have the same number, if that is not exactly the same thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would it be possible that the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. number was on the original document both at the moment when it was not signed yet, and perhaps later on, when it was signed? Your question suggests that the number in the bottom, 00284231, is a number which has been put on the document by the Prosecution. And perhaps we'll first clarify whether this is true or not. I mean, if it's a -- well, it's a hospital number or something like that, then of course it would be totally different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've been patiently listening to my learned colleague. Perhaps at this stage I could say a few words that might clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My friend has been served with some statements from this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- including a statement dated the 12th of November, 1995. Attached to that statement is the second version of this medical report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By "second version," I mean the second copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The statement to which I refer in English contains the ERN number 00361059, and it goes through to 00361064. And indeed, that last page is this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the numbering -- am I right in understanding that the numbering at the bottom of the page is not the Prosecution's numbering, or at least these are not the ERN numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. President. I can assure you that the number at the top identifies it as being part of that statement which was served on my -- on the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's one of our problems, is that the Chamber is provided with the first page with a sticker on it, and I'm afraid that it just hides the -- perhaps the ERN number, which might be under the sticker. But I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's just one other observation that I would make at this stage, that the copy which bears the ERN number to which I've just referred, that is, the copy which was part of the statement of the 12th of November, 1995, bears signatures in the bottom right-hand corner which I think can be assisted by evidence from the witness. But I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would it be convenient if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would please clarify it. If, of course, from the written statement of the witness, this problem in the written -- in the previous statement of the witness, this problem would find its clarification, if that would be true, then we would have lost five minutes for almost nothing. If it's not true, you perfectly are justified to raise the issue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. If you could please be brief, then -- since we are about at having a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but the Defence does not know whether these numbers are ERN numbers. But perhaps we could just have some answers from the Prosecution, because that's what we would like to have, some answers about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do that during the break. I'll pay some further attention to it as well. We'll then have a break until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I have some hesitation to ask what the results were of any communication outside of court, would you, nevertheless, Mr. Ierace, inform the Chamber, and would you please listen carefully, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I've made some inquiries with my case manager as to the numbers which came up for discussion just before the break. This is the picture which emerges. The number which appears at the bottom of the medical report, that is 00284231, is an ERN number. When a document first comes into the possession of the evidence unit, it receives an ERN number. If it is taken out and some further markings are made to a photocopy of that document, then it receives an additional ERN number. One may deduce from the existence of these two numbers, that the first number in time, that is the first ERN number, which was placed on the document, was quite clearly 00284231. At a later point, it was signed by the witness, and that appears at the bottom right-hand corner of the second copy. That is consistent with it becoming part of the statement to which I earlier referred, that is the statement of the witness which was dated the 12th of November, 1995. At that point, it then acquired a second ERN number, which appears at the top right-hand corner. That is 00361064. That is a consecutive number immediately following on to the statement of that date in November, 1995. So, Mr. President, that's the explanation for the two ERN numbers and the additional signatures which appear on the document. In a few moments, I will ask some questions of the witness in relation to the signature down the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is that -- is everything clear to you or are there still questions remaining in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me the floor, Mr. President. Yes. It does clear up a lot of things. However, perhaps I might make a suggestion, that in the future, when there are two ERN numbers on the same document, as is the case with the second page here, because the second number -- or rather the first one is invalid, so it should be indicated in some way, maybe be deleted, struck out or something should be done with it so as to avoid any future problems, so the Defence could know with what it is dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... valid any more. Yes, then may I ask you a few questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting, but I should correct something that you just said. It is still valid, of course, because there are two different versions of the document. There is the document which first came into the evidence unit and then the copy which was used for a different purpose. That is signed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But of course the validity has another meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But at least to make clear what the numbers are, old numbers, new numbers and for what reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have a few more questions to you in this respect, Mr. Ierace. In the facsimile letter of the 24th of January, you indicate that one of the exhibits to be tendered would be ERN number 00284230. That's the number preceding the number on the lower part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have that letter to hand, but if that's the case, then that would appear to be a mistake. It should have been 4231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't think we have an exhibit which bears that ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then I assume that it is a mistake, that 0 and 1 have been confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll certainly make some inquiries to confirm that, but I can assure you that I don't intend to tender through this witness an exhibit which bears that ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And then I may draw your attention to the list attached to your letter of the 27th of January, 2002, where it is indicated four times that the exhibits which will be used in relation to Witness Ramiz Velic are dealing with sniping incident number 5. May I understand that this is sniping incident number 19?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. That arises because this was initially sniping incident number 5, and when the indictment was amended with some changes to the schedule, indeed because of changes to the schedule, it became number 19. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. One of the reasons I'm mentioning it is that, again, I'd like to emphasise that great precision will save us a lot of time. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One remaining issue, Mr. President, I would be grateful if my learned colleagues would indicate simply whether they have an objection to me using the photographs of the vehicle. If they do have a problem, I won't use them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I understand that Mr. Ierace said that he was withdrawing this exhibit, so I just wonder if it is withdrawn or it's not. I don't think one can say, "I withdraw it," "I don't," "I do," "I don't."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the break, Mr. Ierace said that for that moment - that's how I understood it and that's how I repeated it - that for that moment, he has withdrawn any questioning on the photographs in order to give you the opportunity to see whether you would still object after you had studied them more thoroughly during the break. So the question now is whether you are still objecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just have a moment to consult with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only as an exception, and only this time, we shall accept it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, there is no objection against the use of those photographs. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, you still have in front of you, I think, a document -- a photocopy, and you said the first time you saw the document was when you were in hospital. When you left hospital -- I withdraw that. Did you understand the document to relate to your treatment?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand the document to have -- did you understand the document to have come from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Why, yes, because I was issued it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please turn to the second page of the bundle? At the top right-hand corner, you should be able to see the numbers 00361064 [Realtime transcript read in error "00361061"]. Do you see that number on the top, right-hand corner, at the very top, right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the page, there appears to be a number of signatures. Do you recognise any of those signatures?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: In the lower right corner is my signature. In the other one, the one which is very small, I don't know. Doctors', I presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you sign --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ierace. For the transcript, line 70 -- page 70, line 4, says "1061," and I think that is 1064.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's correct. I'll just correct that, Your Honour. In fact, I don't think we need to put it to the witness. That should read 00361064. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you sign -- did you place your signature on that document at the time that you made a statement on the 12th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might that be returned and might the witness be shown Exhibit P3279DD.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you have before you now three photographs?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The top photograph, I think, shows a front-end loader; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but I'd really like to be precise here, because I see that these have numbers 23, 24, and 26. Is there a reason for that or not, or is it simply that we waste a little bit of time? As I'm saying, there are two consecutive numbers and then we don't have 25. It goes on to 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... tendered into evidence, and there might be, I understand, a 25 as well, just as there might be a 27 or a 22 or a 21. So I think it's your intention to tender three photos. Yes. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And Mr. Piletta-Zanin will see the remainder of the photographs in the disclosure in October of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, do you recognise yourself in that photograph? Please look to your right.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the vehicle in which you are seated in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: That is the vehicle that we call ULT, I mean the loader, the vehicle that I was in when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean by that it was that type of vehicle you were in when you were wounded or it was that very same vehicle which appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, my company has only this one vehicle of this type, and I was driving it that day when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Immediately behind the cabin there appears to be an air vent. Do you see that object? It appears to be a circular --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Immediately below the air vent there appear to be some indentations on the side of the front-end loader. Do you know how those indentations came to be there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, this is from bullets. It was all done by bullets which perforated this tin plate. And then here and here, these Plexiglas panes that we talked about. And this is the frame, and you can also see it here beneath the door and over there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please go to the second of the group of three Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. photographs, which shows you seated in your cabin with the door in the closed position. In that photograph, do you see in greater detail the indentations around the cabin?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you can see these here around the cabin and the doors and the frame here, the frame of the door, and here. Yes, you can see it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the witness just indicated the frame which appears between, on the right-hand side, one large glass area, and on the left-hand side, two glass areas, that is, the vertical frame between the two areas of glass. He then indicated the area immediately beneath the glass areas and then the area to the right of the cabin, showing some indentations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, how many of those indentations were a result of fire that you received at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: As regards the tin plate and these panes, all this is new, because my colleagues told me -- I spent a long time in that hospital, and they changed it all. They said there were 64 holes on the loader itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You pointed out a number of indentations in the metalwork on the side of the cabin and around the cabin, and you have explained that those indentations were made by bullets hitting the front-end loader. How many of those indentations made by bullets were, in fact, made at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't say, because -- may I show it here? It was these bullets here, at an angle, and this glass here is new. And it was bullets coming from here that hit me. It could have been the early bullets which hit me, and I simply flew out of the door and then I hid, as I said, behind the front right tyre. But I cannot really say when I was hit exactly. I didn't hear it. Because, you see, we have an open engine, so it's very noisy, and I couldn't hear it. But all I could hear as I was hiding was as if somebody was stoning, throwing stones at it. I mean, that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of those indentations on the front-end loader before you drove to that area that day to collect the rubbish?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No. No. Surely not. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Then having regard not just to the moment that you were shot but that whole episode on that particular day during which you were shot, were all of those indentations caused by bullets hitting the vehicle at that time, or only some of them?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: All this here, indentations, were made that same day, because the tyres were also destroyed completely, and they replaced them whilst I was in the hospital, in order to be able to drive this vehicle at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Apart from having to have the tyres replaced because of fire received on that occasion, and apart from the coverings in the door frame and other glass areas, did any other part of the front-end loader have to be replaced, as you understand it, because of fire received on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. You can see this handle here, and this is the hydraulic reservoir which allows you to lift and lower down the ladle and close it. And this reservoir has a carrying capacity of 210 litres, and there is something here that's a kind of measurement. But it was all punched through. They could not weld it. I think they had to find another reservoir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the indentations that you've pointed out earlier, they don't appear to be, at the point that the photograph was taken, holes which completely penetrated the metal skin. Was that the case on the day? In other words, have there been any repairs made to those indentations as we see them now in the photographs?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, no repairs. Nothing was welded here. And I could do it if I were given a piece of paper. If something passes through tin plate, then there are these sharp edges around it, and all they tried to do was apply a hammer to smooth a little a bit. And if there was a large hole, then perhaps they applied the machine here and there, perhaps. Perhaps this one, this large indentation, perhaps it was touched up a little, but not those smaller ones, not those around the upper ones and those down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please look at the third photograph, and after you have looked at it carefully, might it be placed on the ELMO? Would you describe what appears in that photograph, please, Mr. Velic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the cabin, and you can see those which I mentioned before, perforated we would say, punched holes. These ones. These ones are small so something was done about them, but these were too big, simply, to be repaired, and they were left as they were, and the door is open.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Immediately beneath the handle, there appears to be a hole. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please point it out?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Was that hole made during the episode when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And that was the effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, going on the photograph, there appears to be a slightly raised edge around the hole. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: This here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: That, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please go -- I'll withdraw that. Towards the top of the photograph, and in particular the frame around the top sheet of glass, do you see what appears to be another hole puncture? And if you see such a thing, would you please point to it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: There is this here in this lower frame, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that caused during the episode when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that completes examination-in-chief, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready for cross-examination? Please proceed, then, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Velic, you will now be questioned by Ms. Pilipovic, who is on the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Velic.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have told us that you lived at Cengic Vila. Could you tell us is Mese Selimovica Street still called that or does it have a new name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Its name now is the Mese Selimovica Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what was its name before?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. They changed the name a long time ago. It was called the 6th Proletarian Brigade Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far was your workplace from where you lived?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, my company was located in Blagoje Parovic Street, which means a couple of minutes on foot. It took me several minutes to walk there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long were you working with the ULT 150 front-loader vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Since 1972.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993 and 1994, did you drive this particular front loader?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, yes, I did, up until the time I was wounded, but in 1994 and 1995, I was on sick leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992 and 1993, did your -- did you have a work obligation in -- within your company?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether, apart from collecting the rubbish in town with your front-loader vehicle, whether you ever used it for any other purposes, except for loading up rubbish?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Up until I was wounded, I had a work obligation to dig trenches, to help the soldiers in the Bosnian army dig trenches. So that's what I did with my loader because that was one of my duties, assigned me by the civil defence authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, which localities you went to with your front loader in 1992, to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, not with the front loader. I went to do this manual work. I did it by hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. You had -- you had a machine?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I had a pick and shovel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I see. So if I understand you correctly, you did not use your front loader to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't. We just used a pick and shovel, and we would go off during the night, one by one, to do the work.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20 -- I apologise, let me just check the date. In November, when you were wounded, could you tell me, please, what route you took from your company location to the place or rather the Brace Ribara Street?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll be happy to do so. It's quite easy. If I had a map, this would help me. If you're well acquainted with the town, then my company is located in Blagoje Parovic Street towards the bakery, and you cross the bridge at Malta. We didn't dare go straight ahead so we had to go down the Miljacka River and then right into Brace Ribara Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1992 and 1993, how often did you come into that part of town? When I say "how often," was it every week or every month, and if so, how many times a week and how many times a month?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, as it was -- there was shooting going on, I didn't go out, so that was the first day that I went to that locality to clear up the rubbish.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you were given your assignment to go to that particular spot, did you know whether there were any soldiers in that part of town and whether you knew about a confrontation line anywhere there or a front line? Do you know where the front line went?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, we thought that the front line was Vrace. That we knew. Now, how far down below that it went, I don't know, the front line. But I didn't know there were any soldiers there, no. I knew that our army was there but that was further off. That was quite a long way off.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know whether, at the spot you parked your loader to load up the rubbish, whether there were any soldiers in that part of town, in that locality?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, there weren't. I don't really know because it was the first time I had gone there. I don't think there was, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you explained to us the locality on the photograph and you pointed out the MUP school, the police academy, could you tell us, please, looking at the spot you were wounded at, and the area you thought you were shot at, could you tell us the distance between where you were wounded from the direction in which the shot was fired or the place from which the shot was fired? Could you give us a rough estimate of the distance?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, let me explain this to you in greater length -- at greater length. When I went to hospital, when I was wounded, as the machine was destroyed, the vehicle was destroyed, its wheels and its tyres - my colleagues told me that from work when I left hospital, they said that the machine had been destroyed - they also told me that some French - what were they called - small APCs, with very precise optic sights, precision optic sights, and that they helped them pull the vehicle out and replace the tyres on the loader, and then they took the loader back to our company, and that the soldiers, the UN French troops, there was a driver with them, one of our people who knew French, who could speak French well, and they said that looking through this optic sight, they saw a sniper nest to the right of the MUP, lower down in the meadow, and that they could have shot and targeted that sniper nest had they had orders to do so. But as they did not have orders, they didn't shoot, but they said that it was 350 metres as the crow flies. That's what they said, at least.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you have just told us that the distance -- that is to say that an UNPROFOR team went to the spot where the incident had taken place and made a report with respect to the incident?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, because without UNPROFOR's help we would not have been able to pull out the loader. It was a dangerous spot. It was constantly -- it could constantly have been targeted. So they helped us to pull out the front loader, and I suppose they didn't dare shoot on that second day because they knew what they had done the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear whether they had drawn up a report about the incident and whether they had ascertained the direction and place that the bullet had come from? Do you happen to know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: All I know is what my colleagues and what my boss told me and what Alija told me. I know nothing about the minutes or the report that was drawn up. I don't know anything about that, whether they did or didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: After you left hospital, did you personally, or any of your fellow workers, report the incident to any of the authorities in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I didn't. Now, whether my work organisation did or not, I don't know. It was wartime, you see, so I didn't ask for any damages or anything. In fact, my company didn't pay in their -- the insurance fees. You didn't know whether you'd be alive today and dead tomorrow, what, so you couldn't think about things like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, on photograph 3244 --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I should like to ask the usher to show the witness photograph 3244, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, on this photograph, where you can see yourself, you said that behind the white apartment block is the Grbavica stadium?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: It's not the stadium. It's the MUP school, and I have marked that. So it's the area around the MUP school, whereas the stadium is in this greenery here and you can't see it from the woods and leaves, and down below, you have the stands.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the following? The stands that you can see here, do you happen to know whether this part, the stands, was the front line there, and if so, whose army manned it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I came this close during the war. I was quite close when I was digging trenches during the night, but that was the first time ever during those war years that I came to that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. spot, and when there was fighting at the Grbavica stadium, I know that quite a lot of soldiers died during the battle at this auxiliary stadium which was over here, whereas the front line, which I knew they held, was higher up and seemed to sort of stretch transversely. That's what I was told. I wasn't interested in it myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, fighting was going on for control of the stadium; is that right? Could you tell us when this was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I think it was in 1992 but I'm not quite sure. Perhaps October.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: May we agree, then, that the area where you can see the stands was the area which was under the control of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, it was not. There was a road here and a tram. That certainly wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to the spot yourself and see it or do you just happen to know on the basis of what you heard?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Only on the basis of what I heard from others, but I didn't go myself. I didn't go further than this corner myself. I didn't go that way at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Velic, when you said that you had come from where your company was located to the spot where you loaded up the rubbish, could you tell us, please, whether on that particular day there was any fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, it was in the morning. I left at around 9.00 a.m., and you could hear something here and there. Whether there was a ceasefire of any -- a lull, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often would you cross the bridge that you said was called Malta?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Up until then, not once. I would bypass it, because it was a dangerous area. The bridge was a danger point. After I left hospital until I had been -- and I didn't cross the bridge at all until I had been wounded. I had no need to cross it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've just said that it was dangerous to go towards the Elektroprivreda building. What do you mean? Were there any soldiers on the Elektroprivreda building?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know, but it was an open space from Vrace, and whenever you had these wide open spaces, you were wide open to sniper fire. So people would put up some blankets or cloth, curtains, to sort of shield the area off.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said "blankets," could you explain to us where the blankets were set up? Were they on the side of the Elektroprivreda building?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but they were also put up at the spot where I was wounded. There were blankets there too. They were stretched this way. There was a wire from this balcony hinged up to that balcony there, and then they put some blankets over the wire. But I was there for a very short space of time. I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, would you think it appropriate, for the benefit of the transcript, for the areas which the witness points out to be articulated? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please, in order to better understand when we read the transcript later, point out, I think, what was indicated by the witness on document P3244.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Could the witness just explain, looking at this photograph, where the blankets were and where this protection or shield from the snipers was set up. Could he draw it into the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, may I ask you, if you are able to, to mark in the spots that you said where the stalls were, stands were, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you want me to draw in? The stands?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the stands, and the small stadium where there was fighting, to the best of your recollection and knowledge.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The stadium was right behind here, the small stadium.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, looking at the building on the right, what direction did the stadium take?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The stadium was like this. I'll draw it in for you. But down below. It sloped downwards. These woods, these trees, are up above, so the stadium was down below.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now show us the protective covering that was used, and how high were these protective coverings placed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I came along this street, turned round, and as far as I remember, there was a wire attached from this balcony across the street, and it would be lower at one point. So the building provided cover for one part. It might have provided cover for me had I not come right out with my front loader.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please draw in the wire.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: This is the wire, which rises quite high and is joined to the balcony. The wire stretched across the street. It was one metre above the road surface and then was pitched up rather high. It was between two buildings, from this building here to that building there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you draw in the height of the wire on the building, please. How high was the wire on the building?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: The line would be a metre up from the road surface, and then it would rise to over two and a half metres. There weren't any blankets over the top part of the wire, just the part covering the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you were standing behind this line with your front loader.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark in the spot where your front loader was.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: I've already done that on the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: You can't see it on this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us, please, in the part of town where you lived - and you said that part of town was called Cengic Vila - whether in your part of town there was any armed combat.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: No, there wasn't. There was shelling, though. My area wasn't exposed to sniper fire, but it was exposed to shelling.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that you had gone off to dig trenches up at the front lines, could you tell us, please, what part of town that was in 1992. Where did you dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: Well, that's quite easy. I can do that. One was at Zuca, and twice I was in Vogosce, in Barice, by the communications faculty, and once I was at Barice.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During 1992 and 1993, in the part of town that you yourself lived and in the places where you went to dig trenches, was there any armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ VELIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, in my district there was not. There were no snipers, only shelling, in my area. However, when I went to dig trenches, there would always be sporadic gunfire. That's what the soldiers said, the soldiers in the trenches. They would say "sporadic gunfire." There was shelling on one occasion at Zuca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, we're quite close to a quarter to 2.00. If there would be a suitable moment to stop, then ... This would be the moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this would be an opportune moment. I have another 20 minutes of cross-examination otherwise, but I think I'll get through it in less time than the examination-in-chief took. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just for clarity of the record, when the witness was shown during cross-examination document P3244, the line marked in front of his legs indicates the line of the -- the line he talked about in respect of the line coming from a building and being a line over the street, and the oval-shaped marking indicates the stadium, which is partly behind the trees. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Then, Mr. Velic, the cross-examination will continue, presumably for some 20 minutes tomorrow.
